1200:
** δεσμο-φύλαξ** [ῠ], ακος, ὁ,
**gaoler**, {{NT+1st c.BC+|“BGU” 1138.12 (1st c.BC), NT.Act.16.23, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Tox.” 30, 2nd c.AD: Artemidorus Daldianus Onirocriticus 2.60.}}
1201:
** δεσμ-ωτήριον**, τό,
**prison,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.60, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 486a, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 9.60, etc.; δ. ἀνδρῶν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.23}}: _plural_, = Latin _ergastula,_ {{Refs 1st c.AD+|1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Tiberius Gracchus” 8.}}
1205:
** δεῦτε**,
_adverb_, as _plural_ of δεῦρο, **come hither!** in {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus with _plural_ _imperative_ (except δεῦτ᾽ ἄγε Φαιήκων ἡγήτορες 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.11), either expressed, δεῦτ᾽ ἄγετ᾽ 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.350, +others; or understood, δεῦτε, φίλοι 13.481; δεῦθ᾽, ἵνα.. ἴδησθε 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.30}}: rarely in Lyric poetry, {{Refs 7th c.BC+|7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 60,65, and Trag., δεῦτε, λείπετε στέγος 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 894}}: in later Prose, δ. οἰκοδομήσωμεν {{LXX+NT+1st c.AD+|LXX.Gen.11.4; δ. ἴδετε NT.Matt.28.6; δ. καὶ ἀκούσατε 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 3.23.6; δ. πρός τινα 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Coriolanus” 33.}}
1206:
** δευτερ-αῖος**, α, ον,
**on the second day,** usually agreeing with the subject of the Verb, δ. ἐκ τοῦ Ἀθηναίων ἄστεος ἦν ἐν Σπάρτῃ {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.106, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.2.2, etc.}}; also τῇ δ. (i.e. ἡμέρᾳ) {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.113.}}
1207:
** δευτερό-πρωτον** σάββατον, τό,
probably corrupt in {{NT|NT.Luke.6.1 (no explanation is satisfactory)}}.
1214:
**Δημᾶς**, ὁ
(perh. contracted from Δημήτριος),
**Demas**, a companion of St. Paul: Col.4:14, Phm 24, 2Ti.4:10.†
(From Abbott-Smith. LSJ has no entry)
1216:
**Δημήτριος**, -ου, ὁ
**Demetrius**;
1. a silversmith, Act.19:24 38.
2. A Christian disciple, III Jn 12.†
(From Abbott-Smith. LSJ has no entry)
1220:
** δηνάριον**, τό,
= Latin _denarius_ (usually represented by δραχμή (which see)), {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 1.4.16, “Placita Philosophorum” 4.11.5, etc.}}; = **one tetradrachm,** {{Refs 4th c.AD+|PLond. 2.248.20 (4th c.AD), “POxy.” 1431.3 (4th c.AD).}}
1226:
** διαβεβαι-όω**,
**confirm,** ὑπόληψιν {{Refs 3rd c.AD+|3rd c.AD(?): Diogenes Laertius 8.70}}:—usually _middle_ **διαβεβαι-όομαι**, **maintain strongly, affirm, confirm,** {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 17.30; οἱ πρεσβύτεροι δ. οὐδέν 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1389b16; δ. γεγονέναι τι 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 13.90, cf. Aristeas 99, 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 2.39, “BGU” 19i17 (2nd c.AD), “POxy.” 67.10 (4th c.AD)}}; **to be positive,** περί τινος {{Refs 2nd c.BC+|2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 12.12.6, 2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “Πυρρώνειοι ὑποτυπώσεις” 1.191}}:—_passive_, {{Refs 1st c.BC+|1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 1.226S., “Sign.” 17.}}
1229:
** διαγγ-έλλω**,
_future_ -ελῶ: _aorist_ διήγγειλα {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.6.2}}:—**give notice by a messenger,** with _dative_, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.73, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus [same place], etc.; δ. εἰς.. [prev. author] “Mem.” 3.11.3}}; πρός τινα Philipp. cited in {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 12.16}}: generally, **noise abroad, proclaim,** δ. ὅτι.. {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 5.3}}; τι {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 436, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 317a}}: with _infinitive_, **order** to do, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 353}}:—_middle_, **pass** the word of command **from man to man,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.4.36.}}
1232:
** διαγνωρ-ίζω**,
**make known,** τί τινι {{NT|NT.Luke.2.15 (variant)}}; **speak publicly,** περί τινος {{Refs|[prev. work] 17.}}
1234:
** διαγογγύζω**,
**mutter** or **murmur among themselves,** κατά τινος {{LXX|LXX.Exo.16.7}}; ἐπί τινι{{LXX+NT+3rd c.AD+|LXX.Num.14.2: _absolutely_, NT.Luke.15.2, 19.7, 3rd c.AD: Heliodorus Scriptor Eroticus 7.27.}}
1235:
** διαγρηγορέω**,
**start into full wakefulness,** {{NT|NT.Luke.9.32}}; **keep awake,** πάσης τῆς νυκτὸς ἐν φροντίσιν καὶ δέει δ. {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Herodianus Grammaticus 3.4.4.}}
1250:
** διᾱκόσι-οι**,
_Ionic dialect_ **διηκ-**, αι, α, **two hundred,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.193, etc.: _sing._ with Noun of multitude, δ. ἵππος}} **two hundred** horse, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.62}}; see at {διακάτιοι}.
1251:
** διᾰκούω**,
_future_ **-ακούσομαι**{{NT|NT.Act.23.35}}:—**hear out** or **to the end,** τι {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 11.1; πάντα 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Ἐπιτρέποντες” 471}}: _absolutely_, of a court, **try out** a case, {{Refs|“OGI” 335.71 (Pergam.)}}; **hear** or **learn** from another, τινὸς ἄττα {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Epistulae” 338d; παρά τινος 4th c.BC: Theopompus Historicus 244; δ. τά δόξαντα τοῖς ἄρχουσιν 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1273a10: with _genitive_ _of things_, [λόγων] 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Parmenides” 126c; τῶν λεγομένων 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 6.58.8; περί τινος [prev. author] 3.15.4}}: with _genitive_ _person_, of parties to a dispute, {{NT+2nd c.BC+|“SIG” 599.20 (from Priene), 685.29 (from Crete), “PGrenf.” 1.11i8 (2nd c.BC), NT.Act.[same place], etc.; δ. μου πρὸς αὐτούς “BGU” 168.28 (2nd c.AD),compare “PLond.” 3.924.16 (2nd c.AD)}}; also, **to be a hearer** or **disciple of,** {{Refs 1st c.BC+|1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 1.96S., 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Cicero” 4; τὰ γεωμετρικά τινος 3rd c.AD(?): Diogenes Laertius 8.86: _absolutely_, 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Herc.” 862.3.}}
1254:
** διακωλ-ύω** [ῡ],
**hinder, prevent,** τινὰ μὴ ποιεῖν {{NT+5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.144, compare 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 20.36; δ. σε ὀρφανὸν εἶναι 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 148; δ. τὰ ἱερὰ μὴ γίγνεσθαι 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.82; δ. ἄδικα γίγνεσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 31e; δ. τινά 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.92, NT.Matt.3.14}}; δ. τινά τι (i.e. ποιεῖν) {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Epistulae” 315d; δ. τινά τινος 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 20.79; δ. φόνον 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1771 (Lyric poetry); δ. τὸ πρᾶγμα 5th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Comicus 3, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1159b6}}:—_passive_, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.101; διακωλυθεὶς τοῦ σκοποῦ τυχεῖν 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 3.2.7: ἂ διεκωλύθη (i.e. ποιεῖν) 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.60.}}
1265:
** διαμένω**,
_future_ **-μενῶ**{{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus [265] (probably), 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Ἐπιτρέποντες” 513}}: _aorist_ **-έμεινα**{{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.15}}: _perfect_ **-μεμένηκα**{{Refs 2nd c.BC+|2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.55.1}}:—**continue, persist,** of disease, τοῖσι παιδίοισι {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἀφορισμοί” 3.28; διαμένει ἔτι καὶ νῦν τοῖς βασιλεῦσιν ἡ πολυδωρία 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.2.7}}: _absolutely_, **keep,** of seeds, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 7.5.5}}; **persevere,** ἐν τῇ ἕξει {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 344b; ἐπὶ τῇ διατριβῇ 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Apologia Socratis” 30}}; δ. ἐν ἑαυτῷ **maintain** his **purpose,** {{Refs 2nd c.BC+|2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 10.40.6: with _dative_, τῇ φιλίᾳ 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 14.48}} codices: _absolutely_, **hold out,** {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.216; δ. δως.. [prev. author] 4.15; παρθένος δ. 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 4.16}}; **to last, remain, live on,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus [same place]}}; **endure, be strong,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 8.51}}; of form, colour, and the like, ταὐτὸν δ. **continue** the same, **be permanent,** {{Refs 4th c.BC+|2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 34; χρῶμα διαμένον Nicolaus Rhetor 1.28, compare 4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 232.2}}: with _participle_, δ. λέγων {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 8.71; δ. ὅμοιοι ὄντες 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1159b8}}: with _infinitive_, **continue to..,** {{Refs 1st c.BC+|1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 1.23.}}
1270:
** διανό-ημα**, ατος, τό,
**thought, notion,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 7.5.19, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 3.9, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 210d; διανοήματος εὐτέλεια 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.40c}}; **thought,** opposed to words, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 348d, 1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ ποιημάτων” 2.30, 40}}: _plural_, **meanings** of words, {{Refs|[prev. author] “Rh.” 2.190 S}}.; especially **whim, sick fancy,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιδημίαι” 1.23}}; **intention,** {{Refs|PLond. 5.1724.15, etc.}}
1273:
** διανυκτερεύω**,
**pass the night,** νύκτα {{NT+5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.4.3, compare “PTeb.” 268.73 (3rd c.AD): _absolutely_, 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 2.488, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Aemilius Paulus” 16, +others; ἐν τῇ προσευχῇ NT.Luke.6.12, compare 2nd c.AD: Herodianus Grammaticus 1.16.5.}}
1274:
** διᾰνύω**
(also διᾰνύτω {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ichn.” 64, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.4.7)}} [ῠ], _perfect_ **-ήνυκα**{{Refs 2nd c.BC+|2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 4.11.7}}:—**bring quite to an end, accomplish, finish,** κέλευθα δ. **finish** a journey, {{NT+5th c.BC+|“hymnus ad Cererem” 380, compare “hymnus ad Apollinem” 108; δίαυλον 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 825; τὸ ἑξῆς τῆς ὁδοῦ 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus [same place]; τὸν πλοῦν ἀπὸ Τύρου NT.Act.21.7; πόνους 2nd c.AD: Vettius Valens Astrologus 330.9; τὰ προσήκοντα “POxy.” 1469.4 (3rd c.AD): with _accusative_ loci, πολὺν διὰ πόντον ἀνύσσας}} **having finished one's course over** the sea, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 635}}; πλεῖον δ. **traverse,** of a point moving along a line, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Lineis Insecabilibus” 968a25, compare 3rd c.BC: Archimedes Geometra “Sph.Cyl.Praef.”, +others; τόπους 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 4.11.7: _absolutely_, δ. εἰς τὰς ὑπερβολάς}} **arrive** at a place, {{Refs|[prev. author] 3.53.9:}} —_passive_, ὁδὸς διηνυσμένη{{Refs|[prev. work] 63.7}}: _aorist_ _infinitive_ διανυσθῆναι {{Refs 5th c.AD+|5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus}}: with _participle_, **finish doing** a thing, οὔ πω κακότητα διήνυσεν ἣν ἀγορεύων {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.517}}; but πόνοις σε διδοῦσα διήνυσεν **continued** giving.., {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 1663}}: _absolutely_, **live,** {{Refs|Vett. Val. 58.17.}}
1275:
** διαπαντός**,
_adverb_, later spelling of διὰ παντός, see at {διά} {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 11.1.}}
1284:
** διαρρήγνῡμι**,
**break through,** {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus}} only in _middle_, διά τε ῥήξασθαι ἐπάλξεις {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.308}}; διαρρήξασα χαλινόν **having broken** the bridle **asunder,** {{Refs 6th c.BC+|6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 259}}; μόγις ἂν.. διαρρήξειας [τὴν κεφαλήν] {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.12}}; πλευρὰν διαρρήξαντα.. φασγάνῳ **having cloven** it, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 834; δ. τὰς χορδάς 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 86a}}:—_passive_, **burst,** as with eating, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.2.21, 4th c.BC: Anaxilas Comicus 25, 3rd c.BC: Phoenicides Comicus 3, etc.; δ. μυρίων ἀγαθῶν 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 10D.; with passion, διαρραγήσομαι 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 340; ὑπὸ φθόνου 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Tim.” 40; οὐδ᾽ ἂν σὺ διαρραγῇς ψευδόμενος 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.21, compare 87}}; διαρραγείης, as a curse, **'split you!'** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 2, etc.:}}_perfect_ διέρρωγα **to be broken** or **torn,** διερρωγυιῶν τῶν χορδῶν {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phd.” [same place]; ἀκεσαμένη τὸ διερρωγός 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 623a18; ὑπόδημα δ. 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.82b}}: later _perfect_ _participle_ _passive_ διερρηγμένος {{Refs 4th c.AD+|4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “Orationes” 2.64c.}}
1285:
** διασᾰφ-έω**,
**make quite clear, show plainly,** ἐλπίδας οὔσας κενάς {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 398}}; τι {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 916e, 1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ παρρησίας” p.13O., etc.; δ. εἴτε.. εἴτε μή 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 348b, compare 1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ ποιημάτων” 5.13}}; also δ. περί τινος **make a clear statement** about.., {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Anima” 404b1; δ. εἰς Καρχηδόνα περί τινος}}**send clear information..,** {{Refs 2nd c.BC+|2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.87.4; δ. ὑπέρ τινος [prev. author] 2.19.13}}; **instruct plainly,** ἵνα.. {{LXX+3rd c.BC+|[prev. author] 4.26.3, LXX.2Mac.1.18; ὅπως “PEleph.” 18.3 (3rd c.BC)}}:—_middle_, uncertain in {{Refs|“PPar.” 70p.413}}:—_passive_, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1094b12, etc.}}
1287:
** διασκορπ-ίζω**,
**scatter abroad,** {{LXX|LXX.Gen.49.7 (variant), +others}}:—_passive_, {{NT+2nd c.BC+|NT.John.11.52, 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.47.5, “BGU” 1049.7 (4th c.AD)}}; **squander,** οὐσίαν {{NT|NT.Luke.15.13}}; **confound,** {{Refs|[prev. work] 1.51}}; **winnow,** συνάγων ὅθεν οὐ διεσκόρπισας {{NT|NT.Matt.25.24.}}
1289:
** διασπείρω**,
_aorist 2_ _passive_ -εσπάρην [ᾰ] {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 748, etc.}}:— **scatter** or **spread about,** [τὰς μνέας].. αὐτοχειρίῃ διέσπειρε τῇ στρατιῇ {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.13}}; διέσπειρε ἡμέας ἄλλην ἄλλῃ τάξας **dispersed** us,{{Refs 5th c.BC+|[prev. work] 68; δ. λόγον 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.1.25; τοὔνομα εἰς τὴν Ἀσίαν 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 5.104}}; **squander,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1291}}:—_passive_, **to be scattered,** κρατὸς διασπαρέντος αἵματός θ᾽ ὁμοῦ {{Refs|[prev. author] “Tr.” 782; πῶλοι διεσπάρησαν ἐς μέσον δρόμον [prev. author] “El.” 748}}; of troops, διεσπαρμένοι {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.11, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.3.1, etc.}}; φύσεις ὁμοίως διεσπαρμέναι equally **distributed,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 455d, compare “Sph.” 260b, etc.; ἡ ψυχὴ διασπείρεται}}**is dissipated,** {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Epistulae” 1p.21U.}}; τὸ διεσπαρμένον δόγμα the **current** opinion, {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|[prev. author] “Nat.” 14.7; τῶν χρωμάτων διεσπαρμένων 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “De Natura Animalium - Ar.Byzantine Epit.” 11.21.}}
1296:
** δια-τᾰγή**, ἡ,
**command, ordinance,** {{LXX+NT+4th c.AD+|LXX.2Esd.4.11, NT.Rom.13.2; ἐκ διαταγῆς “CIG” “Corpus Inscriptionum Graecarum” “Corpus Inscriptionum Graecarum” 3465, “POxy.” 92.3 (4th c.AD)}}; **testamentary disposition,** {{Refs|Inscriptiones Graecae ad res Romanas pertinentes 4.840.3, etc.}}; δ. τῆς τρύγης ποιήσασθαι make **arrangements** for.., {{Refs 4th c.AD+|“PFay.” 133.4 (4th c.AD)}}; πόλεως {{NT+3rd c.AD+|3rd c.AD: Pseudo-Callisthenes Historicus 1.33; εἰς διαταγὰς ἀγγέλων NT.Act.7.53}}; **medical regimen,** {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Rufus Medicus cited in 4th c.AD: Oribasius Medicus 6.38.13}}; ={τάξις}, {{Refs|“Placita Philosophorum” 1.15.8.}}
1297:
** διά-ταγμα**, ατος, τό,
**ordinance, edict,** {{NT+1st c.BC+|1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 2.289S., 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 18.64, 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 1.180, NT.Heb.11.23, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Pompeius” 6, “IG” 22.1077.34; κατὰ τὸ δ. (i.e. τῆς συγκλήτου) [prev. work]12(3).173.10}} = Latin _edictum_, {{Refs 1st c.BC+|“OGI” 458.81 (1st c.BC), “BGU” 1074.3 (3rd c.AD), etc.}}; = Latin _formula,_ {{Refs|Inscriptiones Graecae 14.951.24,25 (from Rome)}}; **testamentary disposition,** {{Refs 1st c.AD+|POxy. 1282.27 (1st c.AD).}}
1298:
** διατᾰράσσω**,
